messages.content: I need Nashville for an operating review Tuesday morning. I can leave Chicago after work Monday, and there may be a supplier meeting Tuesday that runs until 5:30. Show me a practical round trip, but don't book it yet.
What dates are you traveling, and are both O'Hare and Midway workable? Also, where in Nashville is the review? That will affect how much time to allow for the airport Tuesday.
Monday, March 16, returning Tuesday, March 17. The restaurant is in Green Hills. Either Chicago airport is fine. I can get to Midway a little faster from the office, but compare the whole trip.

For Monday evening, the strongest nonstop choices are:

- Southwest: Midway 6:20 p.m. to Nashville 7:50 p.m., $287 round trip with either Tuesday return below. Allow about 40 minutes from your office to Midway at that hour.
- United: O'Hare 6:35 p.m. to Nashville 8:10 p.m., $319 round trip. The drive to O'Hare is more likely to take 60-75 minutes after work.
- American: O'Hare 7:25 p.m. to Nashville 8:58 p.m., $304 round trip, giving you more departure margin but a later hotel arrival.

All are nonstop and the times shown are local.
Use the Midway flight as the outbound. What can I realistically make Tuesday if the supplier meeting ends at 4:00?

Green Hills is about 12 miles from BNA. At that hour, plan on 25-40 minutes by car, with occasional heavier traffic approaching the airport. For a 4:00 p.m. finish, I would target Southwest's 6:20 p.m. nonstop to Midway, arriving at 8:00 p.m. Leaving Green Hills by 4:20 gives roughly 80 minutes at BNA after a typical drive. The round trip is $287.
Is there anything around 5:30? I don't need to check a bag.

There is a 5:35 p.m. Southwest nonstop, arriving Midway at 7:15 p.m., for $271 round trip. It is technically possible if you leave at 4:00 sharp and traffic cooperates, but the margin is thin: a 35-minute drive would put you at the terminal only an hour before departure. The 6:20 p.m. flight is the more practical on-time-finish option.
Agreed. Now give me the fallback if the meeting goes all the way to 5:30.

The best protected fallback is Southwest at 8:45 p.m. from BNA to Midway, arriving at 10:25 p.m. If you leave Green Hills around 5:40, even a 45-minute drive gets you to the airport about 2 hours 20 minutes before departure. Paired with the same Monday 6:20 p.m. outbound, that round trip is $298.
Any useful option between 6:20 and 8:45? O'Hare is acceptable on the return.

United has a 7:35 p.m. nonstop to O'Hare, arriving at 9:20 p.m., for $326 round trip when paired with its own O'Hare outbound. It cannot be combined on one ticket with the Southwest outbound, so booking separate one-ways would total $354. More importantly, a 5:30 finish leaves only about 75 minutes at BNA after a typical drive. That is workable with no checked bag, but it does not provide much protection if the meeting or traffic slips.
Keep it simple, then. Summarize the Midway combination with both Tuesday choices and the leave-for-airport times.

Monday outbound for either plan: Southwest nonstop from Midway at 6:20 p.m., arriving Nashville at 7:50 p.m. Plan to leave the office around 4:50 p.m. for Midway.

Tuesday primary return: Southwest at 6:20 p.m., arriving Midway at 8:00 p.m. If the supplier meeting ends at 4:00, leave Green Hills by 4:20 p.m. Round-trip fare: $287.

Tuesday protected return: Southwest at 8:45 p.m., arriving Midway at 10:25 p.m. If the meeting runs until 5:30, leave Green Hills by 5:45 p.m. Round-trip fare: $298.

Both combinations are nonstop. Nothing has been booked.
